_meta.description: Milestones in Shell's history. The company was 'Royal Dutch Shell' until January 2022, then 'Shell plc'.

milestones.title: A London shell shop
milestones.text: Marcus Samuel Sr. opens a shop in London's East End trading oriental goods, including decorative seashells — the origin of the Shell name and emblem.

milestones.title: Royal Dutch Petroleum founded
milestones.text: Established in the Netherlands to develop oil fields in the Dutch East Indies; it received a royal charter, hence 'Royal Dutch'.

milestones.title: The tanker Murex
milestones.text: Marcus Samuel Jr. commissions the Murex, the first oil tanker to carry bulk oil through the Suez Canal, transforming oil transport.

milestones.title: Shell Transport and Trading
milestones.text: The Samuel brothers incorporate the 'Shell' Transport and Trading Company in London.

milestones.title: Royal Dutch Shell Group formed
milestones.text: Royal Dutch and Shell Transport merge operations 60/40 to compete with Standard Oil — a dual-parent structure that lasted nearly a century.

milestones.title: Global expansion
milestones.text: Through the 1910s–1930s Shell expands into the Americas, the Middle East and beyond, building refining, marketing and aviation-fuel businesses.

milestones.title: Post-war boom
milestones.text: The post-WWII boom in automobiles, aviation and petrochemicals drives rapid growth in refining, retail stations and chemicals.

milestones.title: Brent field discovered
milestones.text: The Shell-Esso joint venture discovers the Brent field in the UK North Sea, north-east of Shetland.

milestones.title: Brent first oil & a benchmark
milestones.text: First oil flows from Brent; the field lends its name to 'Brent crude', still a primary global oil price benchmark.

milestones.title: Saro-Wiwa & Brent Spar
milestones.text: Activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, who campaigned against pollution in Ogoniland, is executed; the Brent Spar disposal controversy also triggers major protests — reputational landmarks.

milestones.title: Reserves overstatement scandal
milestones.text: Shell admits overstating 'proved' reserves by ~4.47 billion boe. Senior leaders resign; Shell pays a $120m SEC penalty and a £17m UK fine.

milestones.title: Unified as Royal Dutch Shell plc
milestones.text: The dual-parent structure is replaced by a single holding company, Royal Dutch Shell plc, completed 20 July 2005.

milestones.title: BG Group acquisition
milestones.text: Shell completes its acquisition of BG Group (announced ~$70bn; ~$53bn at close), becoming the world's largest LNG company.

milestones.title: Net-zero by 2050 ambition
milestones.text: Shell announces an ambition to become a net-zero-emissions energy business by 2050, covering Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions.

milestones.title: Powering Progress & Hague ruling
milestones.text: Shell sets out its 'Powering Progress' transition strategy; in May, The Hague District Court orders Shell to cut emissions 45% by 2030 — later overturned on appeal in 2024.

milestones.title: Permian sale to ConocoPhillips
milestones.text: Shell agrees to sell its entire Permian Basin business to ConocoPhillips for $9.5bn — a major exit from US onshore shale.

milestones.title: Renamed Shell plc, HQ to London
milestones.text: Shell drops the dual-share structure and 'Royal Dutch', moving tax residence and top management to London; the name becomes Shell plc.

milestones.title: Climate ruling overturned
milestones.text: The Hague Court of Appeal overturns the 2021 emissions order, finding Shell has a duty to reduce emissions but the court cannot impose a specific percentage.
